1. PRECISE NEW THEOREMS AND ADDITIONAL PROTOCOL PREMISE

Use the same arbitrary finite game, k-fold commuting strategy, proper
tested set C and p=Pr(win all C)>0. Let m=k-|C|,
  tau=[log(1/p)+|C|log d]/m,
  q=average remaining conditional win, alpha=1-q,
  v=omega_co(G), K=65536=2^16.

Conditional on the complete actual event protocol plus L, there is,
for every positive accuracy, a LEGAL single-game strategy of loss at most

  alpha+K[sqrt(alpha)tau^(1/4)+sqrt(tau)]+accuracy.            (N1)

Consequently

  1-v <= 1-q+K[sqrt(1-q)tau^(1/4)+sqrt(tau)].                (N2)

This holds for ALL tau>=0, including tau=0 and tau>=1, with no question-
support gap, minimum atom or dimension parameter. The square-root and
fourth-root terms remain separately visible; replacing them by one
tau^(1/4) term would discard the near-perfect gain.

A further independently proved greedy consequence of (N2) is, for
epsilon=1-v>0 and ell=log d,

  omega_co(G^k) <= exp[-2^(-75) epsilon^3 k/(epsilon+ell)]     (N3)

for every integer k>=1. If epsilon=0 the bound is simply 1. For ell=0,
epsilon>0 the denominator epsilon is positive. No 0/0 convention is
needed. This is a new CONDITIONAL candidate corollary, not a promoted
claim that the earlier TV-only theorem proved cubic repetition.

Exact additional operational premise, unlike a fixed-H state channel:
for the SAME all-input finite first-success strategy, a synchronized
branch has a unit original-module vector v_sync and bad branch probability
beta_bad. With original unit descriptions a_s,b_t, a common smoothing
parameter 0<h<1/2, and common finite-family spectral approximation error
delta>0, let Dbar denote their approximating pair discrepancy. For
each pair define
  r_st=h^2+||abar_s-bbar_t||^2/h^2.
The actual protocol provides
  ||v_sync-a_s||^2 <=512 r_st+3delta^2,
  beta_bad <=384 r_st+xi,
  Dbar<=2D+8delta^2,
with finite timeout accuracy xi>0. If the synchronized branch has mass

Thus the combined quantity
